title: Severe type 1 interferonopathy due to germline STAT2 gain-of-function
description: The transcription factor STAT2 is essential for transcriptional activation downstream of the receptors for the innate IFNs -α/β (IFNAR) and -gamma (IFNLR). STAT2 is activated by tyrosine phosphorylation, associating with STAT1 and IRF9 to form the Interferon-Stimulated Gene Factor 3 (ISGF3) to effect gene transcription. Loss-of-function variants in STAT2 increase susceptibility to viral disease. Here a transcriptome study is reported on an individual with severe early-onset neuroinflammatory disease and an elevated IFN signature. The individual had a homozygous missense variant in STAT2 and symptoms consistent with a gain-of-function effect.

samples.title: C1
samples.description: Protocols: Whole blood was collected into PAXgene tubes (Qiagen, Valencia, CA). Written informed consent for the use of patient material was provided. Ethical approval was granted by the NRES Committee Leeds (East) (Ref: 07/Q1206/7). Samples were collected and RNAseq undertaken at 10 months (T14), 11 months(T15), 14 months (T16), 16 months (T17), 18 months and 11 days (T18), 18 months and 12 days (T19), 18 months and 14 days (T20), 18 months and 23 days (T21), and 20 months (T22). Treatment was commenced at 17 months of age with Dexamethasome at a dose of 10mg/m2. Subsequently at 18 months and 11 days of age Ruxolitinib was added at 2.5mg twice a day after the RNA sample was collected on that day. Samples were collected and RNAseq undertaken at 10 months (T14), 11 months (T15), 14 months (T16), 16 months (T17), 18 months and 11 days (T18), 18 months and 12 days (T19), 18 months and 14 days (T20), 18 months and 23 days (T21), and 20 months (T22). Total RNA extracted using a PreAnalytix RNA isolation kit. RNA integrity was analysed on an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer. Illumina Truseq stranded mRNA Assay. Paired end.
